records.rationale: This survey identifies multi-agent communication and coordination overhead plus stack-level remedies for latency and economic viability.

This empirical ML-security study contributes transferable prompt-injection, supply-chain, dependency, and continuous-monitoring failure mechanisms, though it does not evaluate software-development agents.
This is a non-LLM multi-agent reinforcement-learning study of autonomous-vehicle navigation rather than software development.
This RTL-generation review contributes compiler-and-simulator-in-the-loop verification and concrete code-generation failure modes, despite not evaluating a multi-agent system.
This conceptual water-engineering application provides no evaluated mechanism transferable to multi-agent software development.
This non-SE comparison supplies transferable planner-executor-reporter specialization, iterative self-correction, and verified-results integration against a monolithic LLM baseline.
This non-SE framework demonstrates transferable staged specialization with external validation to preserve operational feasibility.
This review provides indirect human-adoption context for LLM software development but does not study multi-agent systems.
This empirical SE study directly evaluates a protocol layer that reduces multi-agent failures through behavioral contracts, structured messaging, lifecycle control, and verification.
